question: What is a converter dolly?
choice_a: A device that converts a tractor's fifth wheel from sliding to fixed position
choice_b: A hydraulic jack used to raise the landing gear of a semitrailer
choice_c: A single-axle trailer used only to carry spare tires for doubles and triples
choice_d: A coupling device of one or two axles and a fifth wheel by which a semitrailer can be coupled to the rear of a tractor-trailer combination, forming a double bottom rig
explanation: The manual defines a converter dolly (converter gear) as a coupling device of one or two axles and a fifth wheel by which a semitrailer can be coupled to the rear of a tractor-trailer combination, forming a double bottom rig.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, introductory text before 7.2

question: Before wheeling a converter dolly into position in front of the second (rear) trailer, what must you first do?
choice_a: Deflate the dolly tires to ease movement
choice_b: Disconnect the dolly's landing gear entirely
choice_c: Release the dolly brakes by opening the air tank petcock, or use the dolly parking brake control if it has spring brakes
choice_d: Remove the dolly's safety chains
explanation: The manual states to release dolly brakes by opening the air tank petcock, or, if the dolly has spring brakes, use the dolly parking brake control.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.2.1 Position Converter Dolly in Front of Second (Rear) Trailer

question: If the distance is not too great, how can you position a converter dolly in line with the kingpin?
choice_a: Tow it with a forklift
choice_b: Push it with the second trailer's landing gear
choice_c: Wheel the dolly into position by hand
choice_d: Never move it by hand under any circumstances
explanation: The manual states that if the distance is not too great, wheel the dolly into position by hand so it is in line with the kingpin.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.2.1 Position Converter Dolly in Front of Second (Rear) Trailer

question: When using the tractor and first semitrailer to pick up a converter dolly, after moving the dolly to the rear of the first semitrailer and coupling it, what must you do to the pintle hook?
choice_a: Leave it unlocked until the second trailer is coupled
choice_b: Lock it
choice_c: Grease it before locking
choice_d: Remove it and use safety chains only
explanation: After moving the dolly to the rear of the first semitrailer and coupling it to the trailer, the manual instructs to lock the pintle hook, then secure the dolly support in raised position.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.2.1 Position Converter Dolly in Front of Second (Rear) Trailer

question: When connecting a converter dolly to the front (first) trailer, after locking the pintle hook, what should you do next?
choice_a: Disconnect all air lines
choice_b: Immediately drive to the second trailer at highway speed
choice_c: Chock the tractor's rear wheels
choice_d: Secure the converter gear support in raised position
explanation: The manual lists: back first semitrailer into position in front of dolly tongue, hook dolly to front trailer, lock pintle hook, then secure converter gear support in raised position.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.2.1 Connect Converter Dolly to Front Trailer

question: Before backing a converter dolly under the rear trailer, what must be true about the trailer height?
choice_a: It must be slightly lower than the center of the fifth wheel, so the trailer is raised slightly when the dolly is pushed under
choice_b: Trailer height does not matter for a converter dolly
choice_c: It must be exactly level with the dolly's fifth wheel
choice_d: It must be higher than the dolly's fifth wheel by at least one foot
explanation: The manual states trailer height must be correct: it must be slightly lower than the center of the fifth wheel, so the trailer is raised slightly when the dolly is pushed under.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.2.1 Connect Converter Dolly to Rear Trailer

question: After backing the converter dolly under the rear trailer, why should you raise the landing gear only slightly off the ground before testing the coupling?
choice_a: To make the trailer easier to see from the mirrors
choice_b: To reduce fuel consumption during the test
choice_c: To prevent damage if the trailer moves
choice_d: It is required so the tractor protection valve can reset
explanation: The manual instructs to raise landing gear slightly off ground to prevent damage if trailer moves, before testing the coupling.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.2.1 Connect Converter Dolly to Rear Trailer

question: How do you test the coupling after backing the converter dolly under the rear trailer?
choice_a: By disconnecting the air lines and listening for leaks
choice_b: By driving the rig around a full block
choice_c: By pulling against the pin of the second semitrailer
choice_d: By checking that the landing gear is fully raised only
explanation: The manual states to test coupling by pulling against pin of the second semitrailer.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.2.1 Connect Converter Dolly to Rear Trailer

question: What should a visual check of the coupling between a converter dolly and the second trailer confirm?
choice_a: The trailer's cargo doors are sealed
choice_b: The trailer's tires are properly inflated
choice_c: The landing gear crank handle is removed
choice_d: No space between upper and lower fifth wheel, and locking jaws closed on the kingpin
explanation: The manual instructs to make a visual check of coupling: no space between upper and lower fifth wheel, and locking jaws closed on kingpin.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.2.1 Connect Converter Dolly to Rear Trailer

question: After the visual check of coupling passes, what should you connect next before closing the dolly's air tank petcock?
choice_a: The tractor's parking brake cable
choice_b: Safety chains, air hoses, and light cords
choice_c: Only the electrical cord, nothing else
choice_d: A tow strap as a backup coupling
explanation: The manual lists connecting safety chains, air hoses, and light cords after the visual check of coupling, before closing the converter dolly air tank petcock and shut-off valves.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.2.1 Connect Converter Dolly to Rear Trailer

question: When coupling to the rear trailer, which shut-off valves should be closed after connecting safety chains, air hoses, and light cords?
choice_a: All valves on the entire rig, front to back
choice_b: The tractor's own primary and secondary tank drain valves
choice_c: The shut-off valves at the rear of the first trailer
choice_d: The converter dolly air tank petcock and shut-off valves at the rear of the second trailer (service and emergency shut-offs)
explanation: The manual instructs to close the converter dolly air tank petcock and shut-off valves at the rear of the second trailer (service and emergency shut-offs), then open shut-off valves at the rear of the first trailer.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.2.1 Connect Converter Dolly to Rear Trailer

question: After closing the shut-off valves at the rear of the second trailer, what should you do to the shut-off valves at the rear of the first trailer?
choice_a: Close them completely
choice_b: Leave them exactly as found
choice_c: Open them (and on the dolly if so equipped)
choice_d: Remove them for inspection
explanation: The manual states to open shut-off valves at the rear of the first trailer (and on the dolly if so equipped).
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.2.1 Connect Converter Dolly to Rear Trailer

question: After raising the landing gear completely and charging the trailer brakes, how do you check for air at the rear of the second trailer?
choice_a: By pressing the brake pedal once and driving away
choice_b: By listening to the tractor's engine for changes in idle speed
choice_c: By opening the emergency line shut-off and checking for air pressure there
choice_d: Air at the rear does not need to be checked once the knob is pushed in
explanation: The manual states to charge trailer brakes (push 'air supply' knob in), and check for air at rear of second trailer by opening the emergency line shut-off; if air pressure isn't there, something is wrong and the brakes won't work.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.2.1 Connect Converter Dolly to Rear Trailer

question: Where should you park the rig before beginning to uncouple the rear trailer of a set of twins?
choice_a: In a straight line on firm, level ground
choice_b: Only inside a maintenance bay
choice_c: Facing downhill to make separation easier
choice_d: On any incline, as long as the parking brake is set
explanation: The manual instructs to park the rig in a straight line on firm level ground before uncoupling the rear trailer.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.2.2 Uncoupling Twin Trailers, Uncouple Rear Trailer

question: When uncoupling the rear trailer, when should you chock the wheels of the second trailer?
choice_a: Chocking is never needed if the parking brakes are applied
choice_b: Only after the dolly has already been removed
choice_c: If it doesn't have spring brakes
choice_d: Only if it is raining
explanation: The manual states to chock the wheels of the second trailer if it doesn't have spring brakes.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.2.2 Uncoupling Twin Trailers, Uncouple Rear Trailer

question: Why do you lower the landing gear of the second semitrailer partway before removing the converter dolly?
choice_a: To disable the trailer's brakes
choice_b: To remove some weight from the dolly
choice_c: It is not part of the uncoupling procedure
choice_d: To make room for a spare tire change
explanation: The manual instructs to lower landing gear of second semitrailer enough to remove some weight from dolly.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.2.2 Uncoupling Twin Trailers, Uncouple Rear Trailer

question: After closing air shut-offs at the rear of the first semitrailer and disconnecting all dolly air and electric lines, what comes next before pulling the dolly out?
choice_a: Reconnect the air lines to test them one more time
choice_b: Raise the landing gear of the first trailer fully
choice_c: Release the dolly brakes and release the converter dolly fifth wheel latch
choice_d: Drive the rig in a circle to test steering
explanation: The manual sequence continues: release dolly brakes, release converter dolly fifth wheel latch, then slowly pull tractor, first semitrailer, and dolly forward to pull dolly out from under rear semitrailer.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.2.2 Uncoupling Twin Trailers, Uncouple Rear Trailer

question: How do you separate the converter dolly from the rear semitrailer once its brakes and fifth wheel latch are released?
choice_a: Lift the rear semitrailer with a crane
choice_b: Slowly pull the tractor, first semitrailer, and dolly forward to pull the dolly out from under the rear semitrailer
choice_c: Deflate the dolly's tires so it rolls out on its own
choice_d: Reverse the tractor sharply to snap the dolly free
explanation: The manual states to slowly pull tractor, first semitrailer, and dolly forward to pull dolly out from under rear semitrailer.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.2.2 Uncoupling Twin Trailers, Uncouple Rear Trailer

question: When uncoupling the converter dolly itself (after it has been pulled from under the rear trailer), what should you apply or do to its wheels?
choice_a: Remove the wheels entirely
choice_b: Leave them completely free-rolling
choice_c: Apply converter gear spring brakes or chock the wheels
choice_d: Deflate the tires to prevent rolling
explanation: The manual instructs, when uncoupling the converter dolly, to lower dolly landing gear, disconnect safety chains, and apply converter gear spring brakes or chock wheels.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.2.2 Uncoupling Twin Trailers, Uncouple Converter Dolly

question: According to the manual's warning, what should you never do while the dolly is still under the rear trailer?
choice_a: Unlock the pintle hook on the first semi-trailer
choice_b: Check the air pressure gauge
choice_c: Chock the wheels of the tractor
choice_d: Apply the parking brakes
explanation: The manual warns: never unlock the pintle hook with the dolly still under the rear trailer. The dolly tow bar may fly up, possibly causing injury, and making it very difficult to re-couple.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.2.2 Uncoupling Twin Trailers, Uncouple Converter Dolly

question: What danger does the manual describe if you unlock the pintle hook while the dolly is still under the rear trailer?
choice_a: The dolly tow bar may fly up, possibly causing injury, and making it very difficult to re-couple
choice_b: The kingpin will shear off
choice_c: The fifth wheel will automatically slide backward
choice_d: The tractor's air brakes will lock permanently
explanation: The manual states the dolly tow bar may fly up, possibly causing injury, and making it very difficult to re-couple, if the pintle hook is unlocked while the dolly is still under the rear trailer.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.2.2 Uncoupling Twin Trailers, Uncouple Converter Dolly

question: When coupling a tractor/first semitrailer to the second and third trailers to form a triples rig, how is the first trailer coupled to the tractor?
choice_a: The first trailer is never directly coupled to the tractor in a triples rig
choice_b: By welding the fifth wheel plates together
choice_c: Using a special triples-only coupling method not used for singles
choice_d: Using the method already described for coupling tractor-semitrailers
explanation: The manual states to couple the tractor to the first trailer using the method already described for coupling tractor-semitrailers.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.2.3 Coupling and Uncoupling Triple Trailers

question: How is the second trailer coupled to the third trailer to complete a triples rig?
choice_a: By using two separate tractors joined at the rear
choice_b: By bolting the trailers together permanently
choice_c: By moving the converter dolly into position and coupling the first trailer to the second trailer using the method for coupling doubles
choice_d: By reversing the entire rig into a loading dock
explanation: The manual states to move the converter dolly into position and couple the first trailer to the second trailer using the method for coupling doubles; the triples rig is then complete.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.2.3 Coupling and Uncoupling Triple Trailers

question: When uncoupling a triple-trailer rig, which trailer do you detach first, and how?
choice_a: Uncouple the third trailer by pulling the dolly out, then unhitching the dolly using the method for uncoupling doubles
choice_b: All three trailers are detached simultaneously
choice_c: Uncouple the middle trailer first by cutting its air lines
choice_d: Uncouple the first trailer directly from the tractor first
explanation: The manual states to uncouple the third trailer by pulling the dolly out, then unhitching the dolly using the method for uncoupling doubles.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.2.3 Coupling and Uncoupling Triple Trailers

question: After the third trailer and its dolly are removed from a triple-trailer rig, how is the remainder of the rig uncoupled?
choice_a: As you would any double-bottom rig, using the method already described
choice_b: It must be towed to a shop for professional separation
choice_c: By disconnecting the tractor's fifth wheel only, leaving both remaining trailers coupled forever
choice_d: There is no further uncoupling needed
explanation: The manual states to uncouple the remainder of the rig as you would any double-bottom rig using the method already described.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.2.3 Coupling and Uncoupling Triple Trailers

question: Since there are too many truck-trailer and tractor-trailer combinations to cover in the manual, how should you learn to couple and uncouple the specific vehicle(s) you will drive?
choice_a: By applying the twin-trailer method to every combination
choice_b: It is not necessary to learn any other methods
choice_c: By trial and error only
choice_d: According to the manufacturer and/or owner specifications
explanation: The manual states you will need to learn the correct way to couple and uncouple the vehicle(s) you will drive according to the manufacturer and/or owner specifications.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.2.4 Coupling and Uncoupling Other Combinations

question: What inspection procedure should you use to inspect a combination vehicle such as a set of doubles or triples?
choice_a: A shortened three-step check unique to combination vehicles
choice_b: No formal procedure is specified for combination vehicles
choice_c: Only a check of the tires and lights
choice_d: The seven-step inspection procedure described in Section 2
explanation: The manual instructs to use the seven-step inspection procedure described in Section 2 to inspect your combination vehicle, noting there are more things to inspect than on a single vehicle.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.3 Inspecting Doubles and Triples

question: When checking the lower fifth wheel on a converter dolly or trailer coupling, the locking jaws should be positioned around what part of the kingpin?
choice_a: The shank, not the head, of the kingpin
choice_b: The kingpin's threaded base only
choice_c: Either the shank or head, it does not matter
choice_d: The head, not the shank, of the kingpin
explanation: The manual's fifth wheel (lower) check specifies locking jaws around the shank, not the head of kingpin.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.3.1 Additional Checks, Coupling System Areas

question: When checking the lower fifth wheel, what should you confirm about the space between the upper and lower fifth wheel?
choice_a: Any amount of space is acceptable if the jaws are locked
choice_b: Space is only a concern on the upper fifth wheel
choice_c: There should be no visible space between them
choice_d: There should be at least one inch of visible space
explanation: The manual's fifth wheel (lower) check requires no visible space between upper and lower fifth wheel.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.3.1 Additional Checks, Coupling System Areas

question: Besides checking for no space and jaws around the shank, what else should you confirm on the lower fifth wheel's release arm?
choice_a: That it is painted a bright color
choice_b: That it is disconnected to allow easy uncoupling
choice_c: That it is properly seated and the safety latch/lock is engaged
choice_d: That it has been removed for the trip
explanation: The manual's fifth wheel (lower) check includes confirming the release arm properly seated and safety latch/lock engaged.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.3.1 Additional Checks, Coupling System Areas

question: When checking the upper fifth wheel (on the trailer), what two things does the manual specifically say to check?
choice_a: The trailer's registration sticker and VIN plate
choice_b: The glide plate is securely mounted to the trailer frame and the kingpin is not damaged
choice_c: The tire pressure and tread depth
choice_d: The mud flaps and reflective tape
explanation: The manual's fifth wheel (upper) check states: glide plate securely mounted to trailer frame; kingpin not damaged.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.3.1 Additional Checks, Coupling System Areas

question: When checking air lines to the trailer during inspection, what should you confirm about slack?
choice_a: Air lines should be pulled completely taut with zero slack
choice_b: Slack is only relevant to the electrical cord, not the air lines
choice_c: Air lines should be left unconnected until the rig starts moving
choice_d: Air-lines are properly connected to glad hands, with no air leaks, and properly secured with enough slack for turns
explanation: The manual states air-lines should be properly connected to glad hands, no air leaks, properly secured with enough slack for turns, and all lines free from damage.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.3.1 Additional Checks, Coupling System Areas

question: When inspecting a sliding fifth wheel, what should you check regarding locking pins?
choice_a: Locking pins are not used on sliding fifth wheels
choice_b: Only half the locking pins need to be present
choice_c: All locking pins are present and locked in place
choice_d: Locking pins should be removed before highway driving
explanation: The manual's sliding fifth wheel check states all locking pins present and locked in place, and if air powered, no air leaks.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.3.1 Additional Checks, Coupling System Areas

question: Why should you check that the fifth wheel is not positioned so far forward on the tractor frame?
choice_a: So the trailer brakes will engage automatically
choice_b: So the kingpin will disengage more easily
choice_c: So the tractor frame will not hit the landing gear, or the cab will not hit the trailer, during turns
choice_d: It has no effect on the vehicle; the check is only cosmetic
explanation: The manual instructs checking that the fifth wheel is not so far forward that the tractor frame will hit the landing gear, or the cab will hit the trailer, during turns.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.3.1 Additional Checks, Coupling System Areas

question: When inspecting landing gear on doubles/triples, what should you confirm about the crank handle?
choice_a: It is left loose so it can be grabbed quickly
choice_b: It has been removed and stored separately
choice_c: Crank handles are not used on combination vehicle landing gear
choice_d: It is in place and secured
explanation: The manual's landing gear check requires the crank handle to be in place and secured, in addition to the gear being fully raised, not missing parts, and not bent or damaged.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.3.1 Additional Checks, Coupling System Areas

question: During inspection of a set of doubles or triples, how should the shut-off valves at the rear of the front trailer(s) versus the rear of the last trailer be positioned?
choice_a: All shut-off valves on every trailer should be CLOSED
choice_b: Rear of front trailers: CLOSED. Rear of last trailer: OPEN
choice_c: All shut-off valves on every trailer should be OPEN
choice_d: Rear of front trailers: OPEN. Rear of last trailer: CLOSED
explanation: The manual specifies: rear of front trailers OPEN; rear of last trailer CLOSED.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.3.1 Additional Checks, Double and Triple Trailers

question: During inspection, what position should the converter dolly's air tank drain valve be in?
choice_a: OPEN
choice_b: It does not have a drain valve
choice_c: CLOSED
choice_d: Half open, half closed
explanation: The manual states the converter dolly air tank drain valve should be CLOSED.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.3.1 Additional Checks, Double and Triple Trailers

question: When inspecting the pintle hook connections on doubles/triples, what two things should you verify?
choice_a: The pintle-eye matches the trailer's VIN number
choice_b: The pintle-eye of the dolly is in place in the pintle hook of the trailer(s), and the pintle hook is latched
choice_c: The pintle hook is removable without tools
choice_d: The pintle hook is painted and the pintle-eye is greased only once a year
explanation: The manual instructs to be sure the pintle-eye of the dolly is in place in the pintle hook of the trailer(s), and to make sure the pintle hook is latched.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.3.1 Additional Checks, Double and Triple Trailers

question: Which subsection explains the general procedure for checking air brakes on any combination vehicle, which also applies to doubles and triples?
choice_a: Subsection 3.7
choice_b: Subsection 2.1
choice_c: Subsection 9.4
choice_d: Subsection 6.5.2
explanation: The manual states subsection 6.5.2 explains how to check air brakes on combination vehicles, and additional checks must also be made on doubles/triples.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.4 Doubles/Triples Air Brake Check

question: When checking that air flows to all trailers, what should you push in after waiting for air pressure to reach normal?
choice_a: The red 'trailer air supply' knob
choice_b: The clutch pedal
choice_c: The dolly's spring brake release lever
choice_d: The yellow diagnostic reset button
explanation: The manual states to wait for air pressure to reach normal, then push in the red 'trailer air supply' knob, which supplies air to the emergency (supply) lines.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.4.1 Additional Air Brake Checks, Check That Air Flows to All Trailers

question: When checking air flow to all trailers, what should you use to provide air to the service line?
choice_a: The trailer's emergency flashers
choice_b: The tractor's clutch brake
choice_c: The steering wheel lock
choice_d: The trailer handbrake
explanation: The manual states to use the trailer handbrake to provide air to the service line during the air flow check.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.4.1 Additional Air Brake Checks, Check That Air Flows to All Trailers

question: When you open the emergency line shut-off valve at the rear of the last trailer during the air flow check, what should you hear if the system is properly charged?
choice_a: The parking brake chambers releasing
choice_b: Complete silence, indicating a sealed system
choice_c: Air escaping, showing the entire system is charged
choice_d: A clicking sound from the tractor protection valve only
explanation: The manual states you should hear air escaping, showing the entire system is charged, when you open the emergency line shut-off valve at the rear of the last trailer.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.4.1 Additional Air Brake Checks, Check That Air Flows to All Trailers

question: After confirming air escapes from the emergency line at the rear of the last trailer, what do you do next in the air flow check?
choice_a: Close the emergency line valve, then open the service line valve to check that service pressure goes through all the trailers
choice_b: Release the tractor parking brake before checking anything else
choice_c: Immediately disconnect all air hoses
choice_d: Drive away without further checks
explanation: The manual instructs to close the emergency line valve, then open the service line valve to check that service pressure goes through all the trailers, then close that valve too.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.4.1 Additional Air Brake Checks, Check That Air Flows to All Trailers

question: If you do NOT hear air escaping from both the emergency and service lines during the air flow check, what should you check?
choice_a: That the mirrors are properly adjusted
choice_b: That the shut-off valves on the trailer(s) and dolly(ies) are in the OPEN position
choice_c: That the tires are properly inflated
choice_d: Nothing further is needed; the rig is safe to drive
explanation: The manual states if you do NOT hear air escaping from both lines, check that the shut-off valves on the trailer(s) and dolly(ies) are in the OPEN position; you must have air all the way to the back for all the brakes to work.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.4.1 Additional Air Brake Checks, Check That Air Flows to All Trailers

question: How do you test the tractor protection valve on a set of doubles or triples?
choice_a: Rev the engine to maximum RPM while parked
choice_b: Open all shut-off valves simultaneously and drive forward
choice_c: Charge the trailer air brake system, shut the engine off, then step on and off the brake pedal several times to reduce air pressure in the tanks
choice_d: Disconnect the trailer entirely and check the tractor alone
explanation: The manual states to charge the trailer air brake system, shut the engine off, and step on and off the brake pedal several times to reduce the air pressure in the tanks, to test the tractor protection valve.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.4.1 Additional Air Brake Checks, Test Tractor Protection Valve

question: During the tractor protection valve test, at what air pressure range should the trailer air supply control typically pop out (or move from 'normal' to 'emergency')?
choice_a: Exactly 0 psi
choice_b: Usually within the range of 80 to 100 psi
choice_c: Usually within the range of 20 to 45 psi
choice_d: Usually within the range of 5 to 10 psi
explanation: The manual states the trailer air supply control should pop out when air pressure falls into the range specified by the manufacturer, usually within the range of 20 to 45 psi.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.4.1 Additional Air Brake Checks, Test Tractor Protection Valve

question: What could happen if the tractor protection valve does not work properly?
choice_a: The trailer's tires would overinflate
choice_b: The tractor's headlights would fail
choice_c: Nothing significant; it is a purely cosmetic component
choice_d: An air hose or trailer brake leak could drain all the air from the tractor, causing the emergency brakes to come on with possible loss of control
explanation: The manual warns that if the tractor protection valve doesn't work properly, an air hose or trailer brake leak could drain all the air from the tractor, causing the emergency brakes to come on, with possible loss of control.
source_note: Nebraska Commercial Driver's License Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.4.1 Additional Air Brake Checks, Test Tractor Protection Valve

question: How do you test the trailer emergency brakes on a set of doubles or triples?
choice_a: Remove the air hoses and check for visible damage only
choice_b: Disconnect the trailer and roll it downhill freely
choice_c: Apply the tractor's parking brake only and observe the dolly
choice_d: Charge the trailer air brake system, check the trailer rolls freely, then stop and pull out the trailer air supply control (or place it in the 'emergency' position) and pull gently on the trailer with the tractor

question: When testing trailer service brakes, what hand control is used to apply the trailer brakes during the test?
choice_a: The tractor protection valve control
choice_b: The dolly's fifth wheel release lever
choice_c: The foot pedal only
choice_d: The hand control (trolley valve), if so equipped

question: Although the trailer brakes should be tested with the hand valve, how are they controlled in normal operation?

choice_d: Trailer brakes cannot be controlled once tested with the hand valve

question: What does feeling the trailer brakes come on during the service brake test tell you?
choice_a: That the trailer brakes are connected and working
choice_b: That the tractor protection valve has failed
